subject: NimbusData procurement: instrumentation sampling playbook & temporary SLA exception
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@nimbusdata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nimbusdata.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus SLO questionnaire — sampling & evidence questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our procurement team has a short follow-up on how Redwood measures uptime and latency for the Hosted API — specifically the sampling methodology that backs the SLO assertions we put into contracts. A few concrete asks from the questionnaire (attached):

- Definition: how do you compute "availability" at the tenant level vs cluster-wide? Is the SLO based on successful call rate, or an error-free token emission metric?
- Sampling: what sampling windows and downsampling techniques do you use when computing 30/90/365 day SLOs? Do you use p95/p99 rolling windows or bucketed intervals?
- Alerts & ownership: what alert thresholds map to customer-facing SLA violations vs internal paging?
- Evidence delivery: can you provide a short evidence package (queries, sample dashboards, and retention windows) for audit?
- Exception request: our APAC region onboarding has a 45‑day ramp. Can Redwood support a temporary SLA floor of 99.5% (vs standard 99.9%) during that window, and what controls/tracking would accompany such an exception?

I've attached the Nimbus SLO questionnaire (PDF). Can you reply with the high-level answers and an initial plan for the evidence artifacts? Procurement copied here (procure@nimbusdata.com) should be included on any deliverables.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
NimbusData

Attachment: Nimbus-SLO-questionnaire.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@nimbusdata.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus SLO questionnaire — sampling & evidence questions

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers first, then a proposed evidence playbook and next steps. I'll attach a one-page summary and a link to a shared dashboard invite once the Procurement address is confirmed.

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- Definition: availability = fraction of successful API responses (2xx) per tenant, computed on request count (not per-token). Latency SLOs use p95/p99 on end-to-end server-side tail latency for completed responses. We publish both tenant-level and aggregated metrics; contract SLOs are evaluated at tenant level.
- Sampling: we compute rolling-window SLOs using 5‑minute buckets and then evaluate daily rollups for 30/90/365 windows. For p95/p99 we use reservoir + bucket-specific aggregation to avoid skew during burst periods. No stochastic downsampling for SLO evals — samples are traffic-weighted but not randomly dropped.
- Alerts: we separate "operational" alerts (e.g., sustained p95 degradation) from "SLA breach" triggers. SLA breach triggers are evaluated after a 1-hour reconciliation window and require meeting both threshold breach and minimum request volume.
- Evidence: we can provide Prometheus/TSDB queries, a Grafana dashboard snapshot (read-only link), and a PDF export of the historical SLO timeline. Retention: metrics retained at full resolution for 90 days, rolled to 1h aggregates for 3 years.
- Temporary exception: we can approve a 90‑day temporary SLA floor of 99.5% for the APAC onboarding period, provided we have a documented ramp plan and weekly check-ins; we'll supply an audit trail and a per-week availability report during the exception window.

Attachments: Redwood-SLO-evidence-summary.pdf (summary + proposed playbook)
Related links: https://redwood-inference.app/ma-plans/ND-D-38291

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm procurement email to invite to the shared Grafana view.
2) Rishi to share the exact PromQL samples we will use for audit (we'll include queries and a short README).
3) Draft exception agreement for legal (90 days, weekly reporting, auto-review).

Looping in Rishi and Lauren for the Prometheus queries and legal/ops coordination.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@nimbusdata.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus SLO questionnaire — sampling & evidence questions

Following Soojin's overview — here are the concrete artifacts we'll deliver for the audit and the exact queries we'll use. I've included a short PromQL sample (attached) and the logic for tenant-level availability.

1) Tenant-level availability definition (exact):
- availability_tenant = 1 - (sum(rate(api_requests_total{tenant_id=~"%s",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total{tenant_id=~"%s"}[5m]))) over 24h windows, evaluated daily.
- We also exclude known maintenance windows (tagged incidents).

2) Sampling and bucketing:
- Raw metric ingestion is at full fidelity. For SLOs we bucket into 5-minute intervals, compute per-bucket success rates, and then compute rolling percentiles across the desired window (30/90/365d).
- For latency percentiles we use t-Digest approximations for memory efficiency; we store centroids at 1s resolution for 90 days and then summarize to hourly centroids for long-term retention.

3) Alert thresholds and reconciliation:
- Customer-visible SLA breach = availability_tenant < 0.999 for a daily evaluation AND total requests in the day > 10k (minimum volume guardrail).
- During the temporary exception the threshold is availability_tenant < 0.995 for the exception window. Any potential breach will trigger internal paging if sustained for > 30 minutes.

4) Evidence package contents:
- PromQL query file (promql-samples.txt) with sample queries for availability and latency.
- Grafana snapshot (read-only link) showing the tenant's 90-day timeline and annotated incidents.
- CSV exports of daily SLO evaluations for the requested period.

5) Delivery & permissions:
- We'll grant a read-only Grafana invite to the procurement mailbox. Dashboards will not expose internal IDs; data is tenant-scoped.
- Audit logs (incidents and reconciliations) can be exported as signed PDFs on request; we do not share raw host logs by default.

I'll attach promql-samples.txt now. If Nimbus wants, we can include a short runbook that maps incident types to remediation steps used during the exception period.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachment: promql-samples.txt

From: Elaine Park <elaine@nimbusdata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nimbusdata.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Nimbus SLO questionnaire — sampling & evidence questions

Thanks Soojin and Rishi — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few quick confirmations before we circulate to legal: 

- Please add procure@nimbusdata.com to the Grafana read-only invite.
- For the evidence CSVs: can you include timezone normalization to UTC and the tenant_id column? We will attach those to our audit packet.
- Audit logs: signed PDFs sound good. Please confirm whether those will be timestamped with Redwood's internal incident IDs (we need stable cross-references).
- We accept the 90-day temporary SLA floor of 99.5% during APAC onboarding, contingent on weekly reporting and a mid-point review at day 45.

If you can send the Grafana invite and the promql-samples.txt export, we'll have procurement route the legal template to you.

I'll look out for the invite (procure@nimbusdata.com).

Best,
Elaine Park
